text: Fixed a scoring bug. The flip was graded as a ceiling even on days SPY was already above it, so ordinary days got logged as misses. We also stopped giving the map a free point every day the market didn't whipsaw.
Levels are now graded on where SPY closes, not the intraday wick. Dealers sell rallies into these levels, so price often pokes through and closes back under. That is the level working, not failing.
The put wall is no longer graded as support. The map has always called it a crowd, not a floor, so scoring it as a floor was grading a claim we never made.
The upside line now leads with the brake instead of the flip. Over the first 10 days the brakes held on the close every time they were tested. The flip held half the time.

Every accuracy number now comes with a comparison: plain $5 round numbers, graded the same way on the same days. If the map can't beat round numbers, you'll see it. Because the rules changed, the track record restarts today.

The tally line now says how long the map has been running (every night since Sep 23) and that its record restarted Oct 8 when the grading was fixed. It used to just count from the restart, which made it look like day one.

The ELSE road ('it holds between X and Y') is now the gap between the two IF levels, so the three roads cover every price. It used to be drawn off the pin and the gamma flip, and tonight that would have read 'holds between 776 and 777' while SPY sat at 778.10: the do-nothing branch did not contain the current price.

Fixed the 'if it goes down' line. When the book had no real support just under the price, the map fell back to rounding the price down, so tonight it would have read 'IF it goes below 778' with SPY sitting at 778.01: a down-branch that fires on a one-cent move, and a do-nothing range that barely contained the current price. The down trigger is now the first actual level below the price that the map names, so tonight it reads 'below 775' and the quiet range is 775 to 780. Nothing about the grading changed.

The 'quiet range' road no longer swings further than its own box. It wobbles around the pin, and the pin is usually off-centre in the range, so on a wide range it was drawn poking above the ceiling it was supposed to be stuck under. It is now capped to stay inside the band, which is what a drift should look like.

Fixed the mirror of last night's bug, on the 'if it goes up' line. The up road leads with the first heavy level above the price that dealers defend, but when the book has no such level at all, the line had nothing to name: it read 'IF it goes higher' with no number, and the quiet range collapsed to a penny above the current price. It now falls back to the next thing the road does name, and it no longer claims dealers are braking when there is no level above the price for them to brake at. Tonight's book was one missing strike away from printing that, so it got fixed before it shipped. Grading is untouched.

Two label fixes on the chart itself. The note on the right-hand end of each road is a full sentence, but the space reserved for it was a fixed width, so a long one ran off the edge of the picture: tonight the up road read "dealers buy into stre" with the rest of the word outside the image. That gutter is now measured from the text that is actually going to be drawn in it. And the small "beyond a typical day" line that marks how far SPY usually travels was printed on whatever row it landed on, so tonight it was written straight through the flip label and both sentences turned to mush. It now checks the row first and steps below the line if it is taken. Nothing about the levels or the grading changed.

The three roads always cover every price, but that does not make them equally likely, and the map never said so. Tonight the "if it goes down" level is 763 and SPY closed at 763.23: that road is already running at the opening bell, while a typical day from here is 11 points and the quiet range is only 4 wide. The map now prints a line under the roads whenever a trigger sits that close to the price, or the quiet range is less than half a typical day, so you do not read the do-nothing branch as the default when it is the long shot. Nothing about the levels or the grading changed.

A label fix. The chart's forward half is headed "TOMORROW", and the dashed band that marks how far a typical day travels gets a caption on the same side. When the band runs off the top of the picture, as it did tonight, that caption was written straight through the word TOMORROW and both were unreadable. It now treats the header as an occupied row and drops down a line. Caption placement only, nothing about the levels or the grading changed.

The note now tells you how the last map did before it shows you the next one. The chart has had that row for weeks but the note never carried it, so you saw tomorrow's call and never yesterday's being scored. Levels are graded on the close, so a level price wicked through but closed back under is reported as a hold, and a level price never got near is not scored at all.

Tonight the record reached 10 graded sessions, so this note quotes a hit rate for the first time, next to the plain $5 round-number baseline it has always been scored against. Printing two fractions side by side makes the reader subtract them, and the gap looked like a 17-point edge. It is not one yet: at this few graded levels chance alone produces a gap that big roughly half the time. The note now says that out loud underneath the numbers, and will keep saying it until the gap is bigger than chance. Nothing about the grading changed.

The first level on the down road is finally being graded. The map has always named a level just under price and quoted it in the "if it goes below" row, but the scorecard never checked it, so the most-quoted downside number on the chart went untested for a month. It is checked from now on, but only when it is a shelf, where dealers are forced to buy and "it holds" is a real claim. When that same slot is a trapdoor, where dealers sell into the move, it gets mentioned and not scored, the same way the put wall already works. This makes the record harder to pass, not easier: on the 10-22 map it would have added a second miss rather than a hit. Older maps keep the grades they were already given.

A caption line on the chart was losing a word, and the word it lost was "no". The two IF rows under the map put the condition on the left and the reason on the right, and the reason always started at the same fixed spot on the line. Tonight the condition ran past it, so "it goes up through the 773.87 flip" printed straight on top of "no long-gamma strike above spot" and the "no" disappeared into the overlap. That is not just ugly, it flips the sentence to the opposite of what the book says. The reason now starts after the condition ends instead of at a fixed spot, on those rows and on the LAST CALL row above them, which had the same trap waiting for a two-digit score. Rows that already fit did not move. Nothing about the levels or the grading changed.

The chart stops printing the same price twice. The range road's pin and the first level on the down road keep landing on the same strike, and when they do the chart stacked two tags and two notes over one price as a four-line block: tonight "765 TRAPDOOR" sat directly above "765 PIN". They are one level, so they now share one label, reading "765 TRAPDOOR · PIN" with both notes on one line. Nothing about the levels or the scoring changed, only how they are written on the chart.

Road lines stopped cutting through the words. The labels on the chart are spaced so they never land on each other, but nothing ever checked them against the roads themselves, and the roads are curves that bulge between the levels they connect. Tonight the up road ran straight through its own label: "770 BRAKE · PIN" lost the N, and the line underneath read "wicks thr-ough, closes under" with a green line where the letters should be. Moving the label somewhere else just trades one collision for another in a busy panel, so instead every label is now drawn with a thin cut-out of the background colour behind the letters. Anything crossing it, a road, a dashed band, a box edge, passes behind the text instead of through it, and on empty background you cannot tell it is there. Nothing about the levels or the scoring changed.

Fixed a label collision on the right edge of the chart. The word RANGE, which names the quiet road, was being painted on top of the sentence explaining what the gamma flip does, and when the pin and the flip sat at nearly the same price (last night they were a third of a point apart) both were unreadable. The road name now keeps the row and the flip sentence steps aside, since the header line and the IF rows already say what the flip does.

The gamma flip no longer gets to be the headline trigger on the IF row when it has been wrong more than right (it has held 4 times in 9 live sessions, and nearly every miss was price closing straight through it) or when it sits on top of price. It is still drawn and still scored, and from tonight each map also records the flip three ways so the gap between TraderDaddy's number and other tools is measured instead of guessed.

This changes what gets scored. The map now only names levels within about one and a half typical days of the close as plan levels; anything further out is still drawn, dimmed with a star, but is not graded. Over the 15 live sessions so far, 17 of the 39 levels the map named were never approached by price, so they could only ever sit in the untested pile.

The map used to report one hit rate across every level it names. Those levels do not behave alike, and averaging them hid which one is the problem. It now keeps score separately for each type, and the first read is not flattering: the gamma flip, the level the map scores more often than any other, has held on 4 of 10 tries across the 16 sessions on the live record, while the brakes and ceilings it was being averaged with held 5 of 6. Both of the last two sessions closed straight through the flip, once on the way up and once on the way down. That looks like a problem with the level rather than bad luck, and it is now counted every night instead of being spotted by hand. Ten tries is a small sample, so this is a number being watched, not a claim.

The quiet road stopped being drawn as a straight line. The chart's third road is the one where price goes nowhere, and it is drawn as a wiggle inside the quiet range to show chop. How big that wiggle got was set by the distance from the pin to the nearer edge of the range, so on a night when the pin IS that edge the wiggle was zero and the chop road came out dead flat, which reads as a forecast of a frozen tape rather than a choppy one. That happened twice in the last three maps, including tonight. The wiggle is now a fixed share of the range's height and slides inside the range when the pin sits on an edge, so it always oscillates and still never draws outside its own box.

Two numbers stopped being written on top of each other. The chart marks where the last session turned, and tonight the low (751.76) printed in the final minutes, which put its label right where the "752.15 now" price label starts. The chart read "751.752.15 now" and neither number was legible. The turn markers now stop at the divider between today and tomorrow instead of crossing it, so both prices stay whole. Chart only: no level, grade or published number changed.

A sentence stopped running off the edge of the picture. Each road ends with a short note explaining what happens there, and the space reserved for it is capped so the roads themselves do not get squeezed into stubs. Tonight's up-road note was longer than that cap, because this level is both the accelerant and the pin and the chart merges the two descriptions onto one line, so it ran past the right edge of the image and ended mid-word at "short gamma, so it c". Notes that do not fit now wrap onto a second line instead of being cut off. That pushed the word RANGE, which names the chop road, underneath the new line, so RANGE now steps to the next clear row rather than being written through. Chart only: no level, grade or published number changed.

The map mislabelled which road the last session took. Every night it draws three roads, up, down and a quiet one, and the next day it reports which one price actually walked. The up road's trigger can be any of four kinds of level, but that check only ever looked at three of them, so on a night when the trigger was the fourth kind the map could not report an up day no matter how far price ran. The map drawn for 2026-11-04 said "if it goes up into 755", price closed at 766.82, and it was logged as the quiet road. It also mattered for scoring, because the quiet road is the only one where the map's pin is graded, so a day that plainly trended was being marked against a pin it should never have been marked against. Tonight's scoreline reads the corrected way. The grade already written into the record for that session is left exactly as it stands, miss included: correcting it after the fact would have taken a miss off the published record, and a grade is permanent once the session closes. So the running record you see is one miss harsher than tonight's rule would book. The same fix exposed a wrong sentence next to it: when a session scores nothing, the note used to say price came nowhere near the levels the map named. There are two ways to score nothing and that is only one of them. The other is that every level named was one the map reports but never grades, which is what happened here, and price ran straight through it. The note now tells those two apart.

The scoreline under the chart stopped being cut off at the edge of the picture. That row reads back how the previous map did, one phrase per level it named, and it is written at a fixed size with no check that it fits. It had always fit, because it had never been this long. Yesterday every single level the map named was wrong, on a day the market fell 4.4%, and listing four results plus the count of levels price never reached made the longest scoreline this map has ever written. The last two words ran off the canvas, so the row ended at "1 level" and the reader could not see that the level was untested rather than missed. The row now shrinks the type slightly when the text would not otherwise fit, which keeps every result visible, and only drops a whole phrase if shrinking is not enough, never cutting a word in half. Replayed over all 31 past scorelines: yesterday's is the only one that changes, and it keeps all of its text. Chart only: no level, grade or published number changed.

The scoreline now says how far price closed under a put wall or trapdoor instead of calling it "tagged," which undersold days that closed well below the level. Those levels are still reported and not scored, so no grade or published number changed.
The record now says how many graded sessions named no level it scores. 6 of the 22 sessions since the 2026-10-08 restart scored nothing at all, so the hit rate covers 16 of them and not all 22.

The record now separates sessions where the map named nothing it scores from sessions where it named levels price never reached. The Nov 8 note said all 6 blank sessions named nothing, which was true of only 2.
The comparison with $5 round numbers is now counted by session, not by level, because levels on the same day share one market move. Every session's grades are on a public table. No grade changed.

The record now breaks out how each level type has done instead of averaging them into one rate. Through Nov 9 the gamma flip is 4 of 12 and carries 8 of the 16 misses, which the single headline number hid.
The note now says when the map has stopped leading with the gamma flip. Through Nov 10 the flip is 4 of 13, so the IF row points at another level first; the flip is still drawn and still graded.

The record now shows which road the sessions that scored nothing took. Through Nov 11, 5 of those 6 sessions walked the DOWN road, so the published rate leans on the days the map had a level to be graded on.

From 2026-11-13 the note says when the number on the down road is a short-gamma strike the record never scores as a floor, and how often that has been the case. Dealers sell into those levels rather than defend them, so the map draws them as a marker rather than a claim.
